It reproduces salt-sensitive hypertension, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis with raised renal WNK1, WNK4 and phosphorylated NCC, so it models the dominant form of the human disease at the level of both mechanism and phenotype.

Phosphorylation of KLHL3 at serine 433, inside the Kelch domain, prevents WNK4 from binding and so prevents its degradation. This is the physiological switch by which angiotensin II, dietary potassium restriction, insulin and vasopressin signalling raise WNK levels, and calcineurin reverses it. The disease alleles S433G and S433N occupy that residue, so PHA2D includes a genetic lock of a normally regulated switch. The same node explains why calcineurin inhibitors produce an acquired phenocopy.

nodes.description: A null allele carrying a beta-galactosidase reporter, which separates the two human inheritance modes experimentally. Homozygous nulls have the pseudohypoaldosteronism type II phenotype with raised renal WNK1 and WNK4; heterozygous nulls have neither. That asymmetry is the evidence that the dominant human alleles are dominant negative rather than haploinsufficient, and the reporter also shows where KLHL3 is expressed outside the kidney without WNK accumulating there.

KLHL3 is the BTB-BACK-Kelch substrate adaptor that recruits WNK kinases to a CUL3-based ubiquitin ligase complex. Disease alleles remove that function by three converging routes: abolished WNK binding through the Kelch propeller, abolished CUL3 binding through the BTB domain, and in the S410L case reduced adaptor stability. The protein is expressed where the disease acts, predominantly in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct with apical localization in the distal convoluted tubule.

nodes.description: Both WNK substrates accumulate in the kidney when the adaptor fails, and the accumulation is kidney-restricted even though KLHL3 is expressed elsewhere. This is the point at which the KLHL3 and CUL3 forms of the disease join the WNK1 and WNK4 forms, where variants in the kinases themselves produce the same excess of WNK activity.

evidence.snippet: CUL3 and KLHL3 are now known to form a ubiquitin ligase complex that promotes proteasomal degradation of WNK kinases, which activate downstream kinases that phosphorylate and thus activate NCC.

nodes.description: Accumulated WNK4 lowers the secretory potassium channels of the distal segments directly, independently of anything happening to NCC. It clears the renal outer medullary potassium channel ROMK from the cell surface, an effect wild-type but not mutant KLHL3 restrains, and it reduces the large-conductance calcium-activated BK channel by promoting its degradation. So the segment loses the channels that would carry potassium out as well as the electrical driving force to push it.

evidence.reference_title: WNK4 kinase inhibits Maxi K channel activity by a kinase-dependent mechanism.
evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that WNK4 WT inhibits Maxi K activity by reducing Maxi K protein at the membrane, but that the inhibition is not due to an increase in clathrin-mediated endocytosis of Maxi K, but likely due to enhancing its lysosomal degradation.
